traceroute.title: Network path diagnostics
traceroute.description: When a check goes down because its target could not be REACHED, capture an MTR-style traceroute and attach it to the incident.
traceroute.label: Traceroute on network failure
traceroute.help: Applies to every check set to "inherit". Only reachability failures trigger a capture — connect timeouts, refusals, ICMP loss, stalled TLS handshakes. An HTTP 5xx, a keyword mismatch or an expiring certificate never does, because the server answered. Traces run after the failing result is already reported and are rate-limited per organization, so they never delay an incident or flood a mass outage.

step2.title: 2. Mint an enrollment token

wizard.title: Register an agent
wizard.subtitle: A guided walkthrough for enrolling a deported agent into one of your private locations.

step1.title: 1. Pick or create a location
step1.description: The agent enrolls into one org-private location. Pick an existing one or create a new one below.
step1.empty: No private locations yet — create one below to get started.

step3.title: 3. Run the agent
step3.description: The agent is the standard SolidPing container in agent mode — no separate binary, no database.
step3.gotcha1: The token is single-use: it enrolls exactly one agent, then it's consumed.
step3.gotcha2: The agent persists its identity to /data/agent-keys.json (SP_AGENT_KEYS_FILE) — that volume must survive restarts, or the agent will enroll again with a new identity.
step3.k8sNote: This first run persists the identity on a PVC, exactly like the docker run volume. For a no-persistent-volume setup, read the value out of the file the agent wrote (kubectl exec deploy/solidping-agent -- base64 -w0 /data/agent-keys.json) and store it as SP_AGENT_KEYS in a Secret. The agent never prints its private keys to the logs — see the docs link at the top of this card.
